items.headline: Stocks slip as Nvidia's CEO quits and bond yields climb
items.note: On Nov. 12 the S&P 500 fell 0.36% to about 7,592, the Nasdaq 0.39% to about 25,366 and the Dow 0.36% to about 52,297. Nvidia's leadership shock and a 10-year Treasury yield near 5% weighed on stocks.

items.headline: Jensen Huang steps down as Nvidia CEO; CFO Colette Kress is interim
items.note: Nvidia shares fell about 4% after a much bigger intraday drop, while AMD (+5.9%) and Broadcom (+5.5%) rallied on possible share gains. Its next earnings report is now a key test of the AI chip leader.

items.headline: Anthropic launches IPO roadshow, targeting $70–$78 a share
items.note: It plans to offer 825 million Class A shares on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT. A pricing date hasn't been announced; it's the biggest AI-lab listing so far and a gauge of public appetite for AI.

items.headline: Nebius drops nearly 17% after cutting its 2026 outlook
items.note: The AI cloud provider beat on Q3 revenue but lowered its full-year outlook and raised capital spending plans. It shows how AI-infrastructure stocks are punished when spending outpaces expectations.

items.headline: Hot inflation keeps traders betting on a December Fed rate hike
items.note: Treasuries sold off this week as traders firmed up bets on a hike after persistently hot inflation data. Higher yields raise borrowing costs and pressure tech valuations.

items.headline: DeepMind ships Gemini Robotics 2.5 and AlphaGenome 2 the same day
items.note: Reported by AI newsletters; I couldn't check Google's own posts. Relevant if you're interested in robotics and RL work like your PyFlyt project.

items.headline: Naver signs a $1.5 billion AI computing deal for its Nvidia-Brookfield 'AI Factory'
items.note: Reported by an AI news roundup (not confirmed against a primary source). It's another sign of big money still going into AI data-center capacity.

items.headline: NYC startups raised $216M+ across 6 deals in the week of Nov. 1–7
items.note: AlleyWatch's weekly roundup lists Clark and Logos among the deals. It's a few days old but is the latest full NYC funding tally I found.

learn.explain: Key-person risk is the danger that a company depends so heavily on one individual that losing them hurts the business. Investors often treat a founder-CEO as part of the company's value, because their vision and relationships are hard to replace. When Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang resigned, the stock fell sharply at one point even though nothing about its chips had changed overnight. Companies reduce this risk with succession plans and deep leadership teams, which is why an interim CEO was named right away.
